A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DoRA research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial scientific and structural revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original alignment experiments, benchmark scores, ablations, self-training results, and qualitative examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original pairwise and listwise alignment experiments, robust-baseline comparisons, benchmark evaluations, and supplementary analyses, alongside retained earlier results.

M1.justification: V1 Equation 12 places the classifier-derived aggregate weight outside the log-expectation. V2 Equations 7–9 and Algorithm 1 instead multiply each sample's loss by its calibration factor inside the exponential. This changes the optimization objective and sample weighting, rather than merely renaming the method. V2 Table 4 inconsistently retains the earlier placement.

E1.justification: V2 adds Arena-Hard evaluation and experiments using unaugmented HH-RLHF preference data alongside the retained augmented listwise setting. V1's self-training scenario using only the models' own generations is removed. HH-RLHF, Summarization, UltraFeedback, and AlpacaEval remain covered.

E2.justification: V2 adds pairwise DPO, R-DPO, EXO (labeled XPO in Figure 3), and SimPO comparisons, plus RobustDPO and Dr.DPO in Table 1. V1's listwise DPO is retained as DPO_PL alongside RRHF and LIRE; this renaming is not an added comparator. The appendix RSO comparison also remains.

E3.justification: V2 replaces Pythia-6.9B with Llama-3.1-8B and changes the main augmentation generator from Alpaca-7B to Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3. Reported learning rates and batch settings change. Evaluation expands from 200 to 400 test queries, introduces explicit ties and randomized response order, revises judging prompts, and raises the summarization generation limit from 128 to 512 tokens.

E4.justification: V2 adds reward-confidence regression, reward-model accuracy checks, and policy-distribution analysis across lambda values. It redesigns the component ablations and adds vanilla DRO to the lambda sweep. V1's self-training analysis, original human-policy density comparison, and emotional-capability case study are removed. Training-loss analyses are revised; the pizza example and RSO analysis remain.

E5.justification: V2 Table 1 introduces plus/minus uncertainty estimates for benchmark scores. Checklist item 7 attributes these to multiple runs and limits this reporting to a subset of experiments. V1 provides no corresponding benchmark uncertainty estimates. V2 does not specify the run count, seeds, or whether the reported quantities are standard deviations or standard errors.

E6.justification: Most principal results are replaced or expanded. Mistral HH listwise DPO/DoRA win rates change from 56.5/58.5 in v1 Table 1 to 75.0/78.0 in v2 Table 2 under revised settings. AlpacaEval LC scores change from 5.92/6.61 to 18.80/18.27, reversing the within-version DoRA advantage for this baseline. These are not same-setting performance gains. Appendix RSO scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V1 uses the classifier-derived quantity as a nonunit normalization, E_P[h]=bar h, in its dual derivation. V2 distinguishes fixed calibration from the adversarial density ratio, uses E_P[h]=1 in Appendix B.2, and derives a different dual for the calibrated loss. Appendix B.1 adds a worst-case-distribution derivation, and B.3 modifies the loss definition in the convergence analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statement replace the likelihood-ratio-normalization account with sample calibration incorporated into KL-DRO. V2 foregrounds mitigation of over-pessimism and a modular, method-agnostic contribution spanning pairwise and listwise alignment. This redefines the principal technical contribution while retaining the overall goal of robust alignment under synthetic-data shifts.

C2.justification: V2 reverses v1's lambda explanation: larger values now approach ERM rather than strengthen worst-case emphasis. It adds an UltraFeedback mixed-source explanation for degraded results and discusses offline operation and limited gains in clean settings. V1's explicit KL-divergence and classifier-miscalibration limitations disappear. The RSO discussion newly claims consistent inferiority despite unchanged results showing an RRHF exception.

D1.justification: V2 adds Algorithm 1, pairwise-baseline hyperparameters, and explicit LoRA versus full-fine-tuning information, while expanding the training and evaluation recipes. It removes v1's stated 60k training-query count and uniform mixture-coefficient assumption. The new checklist states that DoRA code is not yet released and promises a future release; neither PDF supplies access to released DoRA code.

R1.justification: The main related-work categories and distinction from noise-robust alignment remain. V2 adds references and discussion concerning DRO over-pessimism, including DORO and Geometry-calibrated DRO, along with RobustDPO and the added baselines and benchmarks. It sharpens the existing contrast with DPO/Bradley–Terry-specific methods and removes the conditional-value-at-risk discussion and reference.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodological narrative, and discussion are extensively rewritten. Problem formulation becomes a separate section, contributions become a boxed statement, and conclusions and limitations are combined. Appendix material is reorganized, broader impacts move there, and a conference checklist is added. Author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: V2 changes the predominantly two-column presentation to a single-column layout, redraws Figure 1, and adds a pipeline diagram and algorithm display. Experimental figures and tables are substantially added or redesigned, component comparisons are consolidated, and the retained pizza example gains colored annotations. These changes extend well beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies the distinction between calibration and density ratios, corrects v1's lambda explanation, and adds useful comparisons and evaluation details. However, Table 4 contradicts the revised central objective, leaving the ablation's tested loss unclear. New claims also overstate the evidence: RobustDPO has the lower Mistral lose rate in Table 1, and RSO still beats DoRA for RRHF in Table 8. These issues affect central validation, so the benefits and harms do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
